Metadata of BayesTools posterior draws

Source: R/draws-metadata.R
posterior_metadata.Rd

Reads and sets the metadata that BayesTools attaches to posterior draws: the elements and lists returned by mix_posteriors(), as_mixed_posteriors(), marginal_posterior(), and random_effects_summary_posterior(), and the draws of parameter_draws(). All metadata are stored in one attribute and validated when they are set; use this accessor instead of setting attributes.

posterior_metadata(x, field)

posterior_metadata(x, field) <- value

Arguments

x

posterior draws (an element or a list of them).

field

metadata field:

"support"

exact support, created with posterior_support_attribute() (or a list of such objects keyed by column).

"atoms"

declared posterior point masses, created with posterior_atom_attribute(); point masses are read only from this field.

"undefined_draws"

a character vector naming quantities whose draws may be NA because the quantity is undefined in those draws (e.g. "correlation"), as returned by parameter_draws().

"prior_density"

the prior density of the quantity.

"prior_densities"

a list of prior densities keyed by parameter, attached to the list returned by as_mixed_posteriors() with transform_scaled = TRUE for the requested parameters.

"prior_context"

the joint prior-density context of the draws.

"posterior_density", "posterior_densities"

precomputed posterior densities created with posterior_density_attribute().

"posterior_ordinate", "posterior_ordinates"

precomputed posterior ordinates created with posterior_ordinate_attribute() or posterior_ordinate_append().

"condition"

the conditioning of the draws: a list with conditional, conditional_rule, condition_key, condition_event, resolved_condition_event, averaged (TRUE when the draws are not conditioned on any event, i.e., the unconditional model-averaged posterior; FALSE otherwise), and, for levels whose conditioning was resolved per level, effective_conditional and effective_conditional_rule. Read averaged instead of comparing condition_key with a literal key.

"measure_unavailable"

a plain data frame with exact columns column, measure, and reason, with an optional declared cause enum; absent causes use an already enumerated reason. An optional diagnostics list column retains compact model probability diagnostics. Each non-NULL cell is a plain list with model_indices, log_prior_probabilities, log_posterior_probabilities, and stage; supplied log vectors align with positive unique integer model indices. A missing log vector is NULL. Stage identifies prior, posterior, conditional prior/posterior, event, or component probabilities. A cell may alternatively contain the existing typed BayesTools_ordered_expression_unavailable condition, with a NULL call, retaining that ordered-expression refusal. Other condition objects are not accepted as diagnostics. The cause numerical_model_probability_unavailable identifies a declared law whose active model probabilities cannot be represented at full precision. The cause missing_source_context identifies a prior density that a transformation could not rebuild because the source has neither a declared prior context nor priors (formula marginals of several models keep none); the transformed values and other metadata remain. The cause random_sd_prior_law_unavailable identifies the prior density of a random-effect SD on the original predictor scale that combines several fitted SDs of its block (e.g., an intercept SD with a non-centered scaled slope), and random_effect_design_unavailable one whose block has no fitted design in the prior context; the SD of a block that rescales one fitted SD has the fitted law rescaled. The cause expression_prior_law_unavailable identifies the prior density of a quantity whose prior has parameters given as expression()s (an expression point or an expression container, including the components of a mixture or spike-and-slab prior): such priors are evaluated only by JAGS and have no R-side prior law. The draws are not affected, and the atoms and the support of a quantity keep their declarations, except on the routes that build them from the contributing priors (formula marginals, transform_scaled), where the atoms and the support carry their own unsupported_contribution_measure marks. Invalid metadata requires recomputation/refitting. Human reason text alone does not classify a measure refusal. Tables use unique column/measure pairs. The measures are prior_density, atoms, or support. Entries prevent stale prior/density/support fallback while numeric draws remain usable. Atom/support refusals use BayesTools_formula_atoms_unavailable and BayesTools_formula_support_unavailable, inheriting BayesTools_formula_measure_unavailable.

"linear_weight_space"

"coefficient" for coefficient recipes, or "formula_contribution" for fitted design rows and compiled multipliers. Contribution weights never pass through coefficient C/A again. Old ambiguous stored contexts must be recreated.

"linear_weights"

the weights of the fitted coordinates that form a level of a marginal_posterior() (a named finite numeric vector, or a finite matrix: one row per draw for coefficient weights, one row per fitted design row for the formula contributions of a formula marginal, where the rows are not draws). Removing weights also removes their companion weight-space declaration. Unavailable dynamic recipes remain in the producer's separate transformation/refusal metadata.

"ordered_source"

internal retained fitted totals, normalized allocations, model provenance and source-row indices. Producers validate its row count and preserve the primitive values independently of effect transformations. Recreate missing sources from the fitted models; shares are never reconstructed from increments divided by totals.

"quantities"

the quantity of every column of mixed and marginal posterior draws: a data frame with one row per column (one row for vector draws) and the columns column (the column name), quantity_id (the parameter_catalog() quantity id, or "" for columns that are not catalog quantities), dependencies and weights (the fitted coordinates the column is a linear function of), and label_parts (the label parts rendered by parameter_labels()). Set by as_mixed_posteriors(), mix_posteriors(), transform_factor_samples(), and marginal_posterior() (whose estimated marginal means are predictions and declare no fitted coordinates); summaries map columns to fitted coordinates and render their labels from it.

"output_transformations"

the transformations applied to the values of the draws by posterior_transform() (and marginal_posterior() with transformation), in the order they were applied: "lin", "exp_lin", "tanh", "exp", or "custom" for a transformation given as functions; absent for untransformed draws.

value

the new value of the field; NULL removes it.

Value

posterior_metadata() returns the value of the field or NULL; the replacement form returns x with the field set.

Details

Arithmetic and mathematical functions of posterior draws (Ops and Math group generics), c(), as.numeric(), and subsetting return plain numeric draws without metadata, because supports, atoms, and prior densities do not follow the transformed values. Functions that need the metadata (e.g. Savage_Dickey_BF(), plot_posterior(), marginal_posterior()) stop on such draws; posterior_transform() (and marginal_posterior() with transformation) transforms the draws together with their metadata.

Operations that replace values but keep the attributes of the draws (x[] <- , x[i] <- , pmin(), pmax()) leave metadata that no longer describe the draws. The metadata record a fingerprint of the values they describe (their number, the number of missing values, and two sums of the observed values), and reading or setting the metadata of such draws, here or in any function that uses them, stops with an error of class BayesTools_stale_metadata (parent class BayesTools_metadata). Subsetting a list of mixed posteriors with [ keeps the list's metadata, with the prior densities of the omitted parameters removed.

The fingerprint cannot detect every change: the two sums are compared within their rounding-error bound, so changes that keep both sums (e.g., adding d, -2d, and d to three consecutive draws), changes of single draws smaller than about \(5.6 \cdot 10^{-17} n^2\) times the draws' mean absolute value for \(n\) draws (about \(6 \cdot 10^{-5}\) for \(10^6\) draws), and reorderings that move draws by only a few positions can keep the metadata. The bound grows with the number of draws: such changes are detected at some positions or for fewer draws (e.g., swapping two adjacent standard-normal draws is typically detected for \(10^5\) draws but not for \(10^6\)).

Examples

draws <- stats::rnorm(100)
posterior_metadata(draws, "atoms") <- posterior_atom_attribute()
posterior_metadata(draws, "atoms")
#> $declared
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $joint_declared
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $locations
#>      value
#> 
#> $mass
#> numeric(0)
#> 
#> $source
#> [1] "user"
#> 
#> $component_probabilities
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "BayesTools_posterior_atoms" "list"
